Subject: Post-call: Dedicated inference capacity & isolation — summary and proposed MAP

Sam — thanks again for the hour today. Quick recap and a proposed mutual action plan so we can get alignment internally at Nexa and move toward a pilot. I tried to keep this tight for your execs.

Key pain & goals (as we heard):
- Latency variability on burst traffic (95th/99th token latency spikes during peak inference windows) causing UX regressions for clinical review workflows.
- PHI/data isolation requirement: must keep all inference traffic for production models inside a controlled VPC and run under customer-managed KMS.
- Throughput requirement: sustained steady-state of ~600 concurrent inference streams (avg 8-12 tokens/sec per stream) with ability to burst ~2-3x during batch uploads.
- Cost target: lower per-token cost vs self-hosted while avoiding vendor lock and preserving model version pinning.

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Dedicated GPU pool (isolated tenancy) deployed in your AWS account via Private deployment option or on a dedicated VPC from Redwood Private — to meet PHI/KMS requirements.
- Autoscaling policy: steady minimum capacity sized to cover 75% of baseline, fast burst nodes for short-duration spikes.
- Model variants: recommendation to run quantized 4-bit variants for high-throughput endpoints + full-precision for smaller, high-accuracy routes.
- SLA target: 99.9% availability for reserved pool + 99th percentile token latency SLO goal configured per-route (we'll propose baselines after pilot traces).

Immediate asks / next steps I recommend:
1) You confirm which purchase vehicle you prefer (reserved capacity monthly commit vs annual reserved contract) — Sam, you mentioned procurement prefers annual for budgeting.
2) Nexa infra to share high-level traffic profile (sample token distribution and burst windows) and the PHI classification matrix so we can script KMS/ACL checks.
3) Internal sync: I’ll loop Ben for ops/acceptance criteria and Karthik for kernel/quantization sizing suggestions.
4) We’ll deliver a one-page Mutual Action Plan (attached) + a draft SLA for initial review by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: Nexa-MAP-20270408.pdf (mutual action plan), Redwood-SLA-draft-20270408.docx

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a 30-minute procurement + infra call next week (suggest Tue 4/13 10am PT).

Thanks,
